title: Blueberry Muffins
subtitle: Tall, domed muffins with fresh blueberries
excerpt: Light muffins packed with fresh blueberries and a hint of vanilla and lemon zest. The high oven temperature gives them a tall dome and a slightly crisp top. Best eaten on the day they are made.

recipe.sourceNotes: Blueberry muffins are an American baking staple that became one of the most popular café items in Britain from the 1990s onwards. The key technique difference from a cupcake or fairy cake is that the muffin method uses very little mixing: the wet and dry ingredients are folded together until just combined, leaving a lumpy batter. Over-mixing develops gluten, making the muffins tough with a peaked rather than domed top.

recipeTools.notes: 12-hole muffin tin lined with paper cases.

content.text: The batter should be lumpy, not smooth: over-mixing makes the muffins tough. Fill the cases right to the top for a tall dome. A high starting oven temperature is what creates the dome: the batter sets quickly on the outside while the inside is still rising.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, buttermilk, oil, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Fold gently until just combined: the batter should be lumpy. Fold in the blueberries.

Divide evenly among the 12 cases, filling each to the top. Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
